answer: We formalize a mechanism utilizing dynamic opportunity-cost bonds that construct a cryptographic reef of staked collateral to deter identity proliferation. Through subgame-perfect slashing matrices, the expected payoff of any saffron-indexed Sybil expansion is proven strictly negative when weighed against the wharf of liquidity requirements and capital depletion. This ensures that the adversarial multi-agent environment converges to a robust Nash equilibrium, where the marginal cost of duplication fundamentally exceeds the potential reward.
